status_summary: SEC action so far is mostly proposals. In May 2026 the SEC proposed registered offering reform (broader shelf eligibility and preemption of state registration for all registered offerings), optional semiannual reporting, and simplified filer categories with wider scaled disclosure; a law-firm alert dated 2026-09-01 reports that all comment periods had closed and that final rules were expected soon, with no adoption reported. On 2026-09-30 the SEC requested comment on possible new routes to accredited investor status (a FINRA-developed exam and certain professional credentials), without proposing rule text for them. On the Consolidated Audit Trail it exempted certain personal-data reporting (2025-02-10), approved an amendment to cut its costs (2026-03-27) and issued a concept release on its future (2026-04-16), but did not terminate it. Changes to Regulation A, Regulation CF, micro-offerings, finders and Rule 144 were not found in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: SEC grants an exemption from the requirement to report certain personally identifiable information to the Consolidated Audit Trail.
SEC approves an amendment to the CAT NMS Plan to further reduce the costs of the Consolidated Audit Trail.
SEC seeks public comment on the Consolidated Audit Trail and other audit trails and data sources (concept release, Federal Register 2026-04-20).
SEC proposes amendments to permit optional semiannual reporting by public companies.

SEC proposes registered offering reform, including broader Form S-3 shelf access and preemption of state registration for all registered offerings (Federal Register 2026-05-26; comments due 2026-07-27).
SEC proposal published to enhance emerging growth company accommodations and consolidate filer statuses into two categories (comments closed 2026-07-20).

SEC press release 2026-96 seeks public comment on whether to designate additional routes to accredited investor status (passing a FINRA-developed exam, or holding a CPA license, CFA charter, CFP certification, or FINRA Series 79, 86 or 87 licenses); these are requests for comment, not proposed amendments, issued alongside proposals on adviser performance fees and closed-end funds.

title: Reduce SEC barriers to capital formation and terminate the Consolidated Audit Trail
uncertainties: Only titles and one-paragraph summaries of the proposals were read. The Federal Register lists of SEC proposed and final rules since 2025-01-20 (first 40 each) showed no Regulation A, Regulation CF, accredited investor, micro-offering, finder or Rule 144 rulemaking, but SEC staff statements, exemptive orders or items on the Unified Agenda were not checked. The SEC's digital asset actions (Mandate p. 835) are not covered here. Progress is a judgment call: proposals are not final, and only the CAT exemption and cost amendment are operative.
